macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stock futures rise ahead of major earnings week
items.summary: Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures moved higher after the indexes’ weaker Friday close. Investors are focused on a heavy earnings calendar, with Meta and Tesla scheduled to report Wednesday.[1]

items.title: Oil decline supports bonds and Wall Street futures as Asian stocks slip
items.summary: Asian equities weakened amid concerns about the funding demands of artificial intelligence, while lower oil prices supported bonds and U.S. equity futures. S&P 500 futures rose about 0.7% and Nasdaq futures about 1.0%; Japan’s Nikkei fell 1.2% after a 5.4% weekly decline.[5]

items.title: Hot inflation raises expectations for further Fed tightening
items.summary: Markets are reassessing interest-rate expectations after stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation. Fed officials are in their blackout period before the October 28 policy decision, while market pricing cited a 14.9% probability of a rate hike after the October meeting.[1][4]

items.title: China third-quarter growth slightly exceeds forecasts
items.summary: China’s economy grew 4.5% year over year in the third quarter, narrowly beating expectations. Retail sales increased 1.1% and industrial output rose 5.5%, providing some support for the global-growth outlook.[5]

items.title: Meta and Tesla headline closely watched earnings releases
items.summary: Meta Platforms and Tesla are the main focus of a crowded third-quarter earnings week. Investors are watching Meta’s artificial-intelligence monetization plans and Tesla’s results amid broader concerns about AI investment costs.[1][7]

items.title: Semiconductor stocks remain under pressure
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 4.5% over the prior week, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index declined 11.4% and recorded an eighth consecutive daily loss, reflecting persistent concern over inflation, financing costs and AI-related investment.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $82,000 as crypto market edges higher
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $82,446, up 0.8% over 24 hours after briefly falling below $80,700. The total crypto market capitalization rose about 0.3% to $2.83 trillion, while Ethereum, BNB, XRP and Solana also posted modest daily gains.[2]

items.title: Nearly $934 million in crypto positions liquidated
items.summary: About $934 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated across roughly 167,400 accounts during the past 24 hours, with Bitcoin and Ethereum accounting for the heaviest losses.[7]

items.title: CFTC proposes voluntary unified crypto oversight framework
items.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission proposed a voluntary Reg CM framework that would let crypto exchanges seek unified federal oversight instead of navigating fragmented state licensing requirements.[2]

items.title: European Commission reviews MiCA staking rules
items.summary: The European Commission is examining whether current staking provisions under the Markets in Crypto-Assets framework are adequate, potentially opening the door to additional requirements for crypto companies.[1]

items.title: Qubic reports exploit affecting 1,404 wallets
items.summary: Qubic said attackers exploited weak randomness in wallet seed generation to drain approximately 2.94 trillion QU from 1,404 wallets. The project said the vulnerability was in seed generation rather than the core protocol.[2]

items.title: Cysic bridge attack leads to unauthorized minting of CYS
items.summary: Cysic reported that its cross-chain bridge was attacked, allowing roughly 10 million CYS tokens to be minted without authorization on BNB Smart Chain. The bridge was suspended while the team investigated database-access and processing vulnerabilities.[5]

items.title: JPMorgan expands JPM Coin to Ethereum
items.summary: JPMorgan launched its deposit token JPM Coin on the Ethereum network, making it available to institutional clients.[3]

items.title: IoTeX activates Zanzibar hard fork
items.summary: IoTeX activated the Zanzibar hard fork on mainnet at block height 53,533,081, with staking rewards distributed directly on-chain by the protocol.[3]

items.title: Visa moves to close crypto payment loophole for meme-coin transactions
items.summary: Visa reportedly notified payment processors that it will no longer accept a payment-code workaround used for meme-coin transactions, giving processors a transition period expected to end the following week.[1]

items.title: Hyperliquid burns nearly $891,000 of HYPE
items.summary: Hyperliquid repurchased and burned about 11,340 HYPE tokens worth approximately $890,900 over 24 hours, while estimated platform fee revenue was about $764,900.[6]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Liquid Swords declares bankruptcy
items.summary: Swedish game studio Liquid Swords has declared bankruptcy after reportedly being unable to pay employees’ salaries for several months.

items.title: FURIA wins Thunderpick World Championship
items.summary: FURIA defeated BETBOOM 3–2 in Malta to win the Thunderpick World Championship, ending a nearly year-long title drought and claiming its second championship.

items.title: LOUD reaches Champions Shanghai grand final
items.summary: LOUD beat Team Vitality 2–1 after a disputed round rollback to reach its first international title match since 2022.

items.title: Xbox hires for physical game distribution role
items.summary: Microsoft is hiring a Games Supply Strategist to manage physical game releases, signaling continued attention to boxed-game logistics despite broader industry movement toward digital distribution.

items.title: Steam sets new concurrent-user record
items.summary: Steam reportedly surpassed 43.5 million simultaneous users, exceeding its previous March 2026 record of 42,686,616.

items.title: New York bill targets game ownership and shutdowns
items.summary: U.S. Representative Ritchie Torres announced the proposed Power To The Players Act, which would direct the FTC to protect consumers’ ability to play purchased games and require offline functionality before online servers are shut down.

items.title: Microsoft announces Xbox Nano Controller
items.summary: Microsoft announced a compact Xbox controller designed for broad device compatibility, featuring a rechargeable battery and programmable action button.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign early access begins
items.summary: Digital preorders of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 provide campaign early access from October 16, ahead of the game’s October 23 launch on PC, Xbox Series, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch 2.
